whatsHappening.background: The Kurdish people are a stateless ethnic group of roughly 25 to 60 million spread across Turkey, Syria, Iran, Iraq, and nearby regions. Their crisis is rooted in the collapse of Ottoman rule and the failure to create a Kurdish state after World War I. Since then, Kurds have faced decades of repression, cultural suppression, cross-border war, and repeated violence from multiple states and armed actors. In recent decades, Kurdish movements have also been shaped by the rise of ISIS, shifting foreign alliances, Turkish offensives, and renewed crackdowns in Iran and elsewhere.

parties.name: Kurdish Political and Armed Groups
parties.description: These include organizations such as the PKK, DEM Party, YPG, SDF, PDKI, KRG, KDP, and PUK, which differ by country and strategy.

parties.name: Turkey
parties.description: Has a long history of suppressing Kurdish language, political movements, and armed groups, including cross-border operations.

parties.name: Syria
parties.description: Kurdish groups in Syria have pursued autonomy while also facing war, ISIS violence, and Turkish military offensives.

parties.name: Iran
parties.description: Kurdish communities and activists in Iran continue to face arrests, executions, and repression.

parties.name: Iraq
parties.description: Iraq includes the Kurdistan Regional Government but also carries the legacy of genocide, displacement, and conflict against Kurdish populations.

parties.name: Foreign Powers
parties.description: Western powers, the United States, and regional governments have all shaped Kurdish politics through borders, alliances, and military involvement.

timeline.description: The Treaty of Sèvres proposed a possible Kurdish state, but it was never ratified.
The Treaty of Lausanne replaced Sèvres and removed the obligation to create a Kurdish state.
Violence intensified across Turkey, Iran, and Iraq, including Saddam Hussein’s genocide against Iraqi Kurds and the Halabja chemical attack.
Kurdish autonomy expanded in Iraq and Syria, but new wars involving ISIS, Turkey, and regional forces brought further instability.
Turkish offensives, repression in Iran, and lingering post-ISIS conflict continue to shape Kurdish life across the region.

civilianImpact.experiences: For Kurdish civilians, this crisis has meant decades of displacement, killings, cultural suppression, political isolation, detention, and forced migration. Because Kurds are spread across multiple countries and often face state censorship, their suffering is less visible and less consistently documented than many other crises. Even so, the record shows recurring executions, arrests, and restrictions on language, identity, and political participation, alongside repeated waves of war and displacement.

image.alt: Kurdish civilians affected by displacement and repression

howToHelp.summary: The Kurdish crisis is often overlooked because it is spread across several countries rather than tied to a single state. Raising awareness matters because underreported repression, displacement, and rights abuses are easier to ignore when international attention fades.

learnMore.text: This slide explains how Kurdistan’s modern crisis grew out of denied statehood, regional repression, and a century of conflict.

whatsHappening.background: Kurdish civilians face a crisis that combines state repression, conflict displacement, and long-term cultural and political suppression. The effects differ across countries, but together they form a broad humanitarian pattern of insecurity and marginalization.

parties.name: 500+ executed since 2020
parties.description: Executions have targeted Kurdish people on charges ranging from political dissent to other accusations.

parties.name: 2,000+ detained since 2020
parties.description: Thousands of Kurdish civilians have been detained, with many formally charged or sentenced.

parties.name: 2 million+ relocated
parties.description: Since 2011, over 2 million refugees or internally displaced people from Syria and Iraq have relocated to Iraqi Kurdistan.

parties.name: Iranian Kurdistan under pressure
parties.description: In January 2026 alone, reports recorded hundreds of arbitrary arrests, many killings, and additional executions.

civilianImpact.experiences: Kurdish civilians have endured not only direct violence but also the slower harms of cultural erasure, blocked political participation, forced migration, and state surveillance. The lack of a unified state makes both aid and public visibility harder. In many places, Kurdish people face punishment for activism, association, or simply asserting language and identity, while broader regional wars continue to spill into Kurdish communities.

howToHelp.summary: Because the Kurdish crisis crosses borders, support often means combining awareness with aid for broader humanitarian operations in the places where Kurdish communities live. Staying informed also matters because documentation gaps make silence especially dangerous.

learnMore.text: The civilian toll includes executions, detention, displacement, and long-term restrictions on Kurdish language, identity, and political life.

whatsHappening.background: Helping Kurdish communities is more complicated than in many country-specific crises because Kurds are spread across several states and do not have one unified national aid system. Still, support for trusted humanitarian organizations and informed public awareness can make a real difference.

parties.name: UNHCR
parties.description: Supports displaced people and refugees across the wider region, including communities affected by Kurdish displacement.

parties.name: World Food Programme
parties.description: Provides food assistance in conflict-affected parts of Iraq, Syria, and surrounding areas where Kurdish families have been displaced.

parties.name: Human Rights Reporting
parties.description: Following and sharing credible reporting helps document abuses that are often hidden or undercounted.

parties.name: Public Education
parties.description: Teaching others about Kurdish history and current repression helps counter invisibility and misinformation.

civilianImpact.experiences: Helping Kurdish communities means not letting a long-running and fragmented humanitarian crisis disappear from public view. Donations can support displaced families and conflict-affected civilians, while awareness and documentation help protect people whose suffering is often obscured by borders, censorship, and broader regional wars.

image.alt: Kurdish families and civilians affected by conflict

howToHelp.summary: Educate yourself and others about the Kurdish crisis, support trusted humanitarian organizations such as UNHCR and WFP that operate in the relevant regions, and follow verified human rights reporting so abuses are not ignored or erased.

learnMore.text: You can also follow Kurdish human rights documentation and broader regional humanitarian reporting to stay informed.
